thread:
liu: Hi, we're seeing a big spike of 429s and intermittent 502s from EU users since ~2026-03-17T07:10Z. Affected endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate - one client reports 200ms -> 3s latency then 429.

emily: thanks @liu, can you paste a few timestamps and a dig/traceroute from an affected client? Also approx % of requests failing?

liu: timestamps: 2026-03-17T07:10:32Z, 07:11:05Z, 07:12:48Z. ~= 12% of requests from one customer in DE.
Example curl response: 
```
HTTP/2 429
date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 07:11:05 GMT
content-type: application/json
retry-after: 2
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "global token rate limit"
}
```
Dig/traceroute from Frankfurt (client):
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai
3.6.123.45

$ traceroute -n 3.6.123.45
 1  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms
 2  52.95.XX.XX  12.3 ms
 3  3.6.123.45  28.7 ms
```
Looks like resolution pointed to a US edge IP (us-west) not eu-edge.

raj: that matches other reports. (reacts :eyes:) Any recent GeoIP or CDN config changes?

tom: we rolled out a GeoIP DB update at ~2026-03-17T07:00 UTC. Deploy-bot logged an S3 GET 503 during the rollout for a subset of POPs. Could be a partial update left some POPs with old DB mapping -> wrong POP answers.

deploy-bot: [deploy] geodb-update v2026.03.17 started 07:00 UTC, s3-sync error in eu-north-1 at 07:02:24 (503), retry succeeded at 07:04:12.

emily: repro from an EU residential resolver (Vodafone DE) shows same:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
3.6.123.45
```
CNAME TTL is 300, so stale resolver entries could persist for minutes. But the problem is broad across ISPs.

raj: immediate ask: can affected customers flush resolvers (not always possible). Short-term: we should enable the nearest-region fallback policy for EU tenant traffic to avoid cross-region routing until DB sync is validated.

tom: I can push a temporary routing override that prefers eu-edge based on source ASN/country header in 5m. Will monitor.

emily: implemented fallback toggle at 07:17 UTC. Within ~2 minutes the 429 rate dropped from 12% -> 0.5% for the reported customer.

liu: confirmed from customer: latency back to ~120ms and 429s stopped after 07:20. Thanks. :tada:

raj: next actions (postmortem):
- make geodb sync atomic (swap file only after full sync across all POPs)
- add healthcheck that fails the rollout if S3 GET returns 5xx on >1 POP
- reduce CNAME TTL during rollouts or use pre-warm propagation endpoints
- surface active geoip version per POP in console

tom: opened ENG-7892 with checklist and remediation steps, including an emergency CNAME rotation plan to force resolver refreshes if needed.

emily: we've notified customer and their packet captures show eu-edge after change. Closing this thread; will link the postmortem when ready. If anyone sees residual problems ping #incidents.
